chapter.overview: This chapter introduces neurons as specialized signaling cells that form neural circuits, transmitting electrical messages to target tissues via consistent structural components: the soma, dendrites, and axon. It details the specific functions of these parts, including signal reception at synapses, electrical transmission along variable-length axons, and neurotransmitter release from terminals. The text then shifts to glial cells, contrasting historical high ratio estimates with modern findings of roughly 1:1 ratios in certain primate regions, while noting regional variations. Finally, it categorizes four major CNS glial types, specifying that astrocytes regulate ions and nutrients, microglia act as phagocytes, ependymal cells produce cerebrospinal fluid, and oligodendrocytes form myelin sheaths to enhance neuronal function.

chapter.overview: This chapter introduces neurons as specialized signaling cells that form neural circuits, transmitting electrical messages to target tissues via consistent structural components: the soma, dendrites, and axon. It details the specific functions of these parts, including signal reception at synapses, electrical transmission along variable-length axons, and neurotransmitter release from terminals. The text then shifts to glial cells, contrasting historical high ratio estimates with modern findings of roughly 1:1 ratios in certain primate regions, while noting regional variations. Finally, it categorizes four major CNS glial types, specifying that astrocytes regulate ions and nutrients, microglia act as phagocytes, ependymal cells produce cerebrospinal fluid, and oligodendrocytes form myelin sheaths to enhance neuronal function.
